key_insight: A multi-agent LLM system can autonomously generate and verify deterministic reaction-classification rules, expanding a chemistry taxonomy from 68 to 14,073 classes without human curation.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, interpretable synthesis-planning systems that can adapt to new reaction space while remaining auditable and suitable for large chemical knowledge bases.
method: LLM agents classify reactions and propose symbolic rules for each transformation.
A verification loop tests each candidate rule against 665,901 US patent reactions before acceptance.
A lightweight fingerprint-based classifier uses the generated rules to label unseen reactions and expand on demand.
evidence_signal: On the patent-reaction corpus, the system generated verified rules across 665,901 reactions and classified 97.7% of unseen reactions, matching a leading proprietary classifier while resolving chemistry more finely.
watch_item: The approach depends on verification coverage and rule quality across a long-tailed chemistry space, so rare or novel reaction classes may still require careful validation and maintenance.
paper_title: Agentic generation of verifiable rules for deterministic, self-expanding reaction classification
